results.fact: Which Nason Ridge trailheads charge a fee
results.correct_value: Nason Ridge and Round Mountain trailheads charge $5/day or $30/yr; Rock Mountain and Merritt Lake trailheads need no pass
results.evidence: The Forest Service Round Mountain Trailhead page states a Northwest Forest Pass is required for all vehicles ($5/day, $30/year), and the Alpine Lookout hike page (which starts at the Round Mountain trailhead on FR 6910) lists NW Forest Pass / America the Beautiful required. The Rock Mountain (#1587) and Merritt Lake hike pages list no pass required; the FS Nason Ridge trail page confirms the $5/$30 fee at the Nason Ridge trailhead. So the Alpine Lookout entry is right and the three 'only Nason Ridge charges' sentences are wrong; they are corrected to name both fee trailheads.

results.fact: Time to reach summit vs total car-to-car time
results.correct_value: summitTimeHrs should not hold the 8.5-hr car-to-car total; nulled (itinerary places the summit ~4.5 hr after a 5 AM start)
results.evidence: The route is an 8-mile round trip (WTA hike page; independent hiker write-up also 8 mi, ~4,050 ft); AllTrails averages about 6.75 hours for the full out-and-back, so 8.5 hours is a car-to-car figure, not a time to the summit. The row's own totalHrs, sectionBreakdown and itinerary treat 8.5 as car-to-car. Per the catalog convention for this defect class, the duplicated total is removed rather than replaced with a computed number.

results.fact: whether the route is ever climbed in avalanche season
results.correct_value: The Jul-Sep scramble season falls outside avalanche season, but the peak has been climbed in winter and the southwest face carries avalanche hazard then
results.evidence: A February 22-23, 2020 trip report describes probable first winter ascents of Cardinal, Emerald and Saska, noting low avalanche danger was important for the steep face up Saska and that a ski was lost over a cliff on the descent. The row's hazards, climate spring and winter entries and descent_text all agree; only the avalanche zone sentence claimed the route is never climbed in avalanche season. Scoped the claim to the summer window.

results.fact: dist_km (35.41 km = 22 mi) shown as one-way approach vs summit ~11 mi from the trailhead
results.evidence: The Fox Camp / Pyramid trail junction is about 8 miles up the North Fork Entiat trail with the Emerald-Saska basin 1.5 miles beyond (summitpost route summary), and a trip report camped near the junction at ~mile 8.5 with Saska about 2 more miles (hike2hike) - about 10.5-11 miles one way. The row's summit waypoint is at distMi 11 and the itinerary totals 22 miles round trip, so 35.41 km is the round-trip figure stored in the one-way field.

results.fact: Fox Camp elevation (waypoint 6,900 ft) vs approach saying the basin (~7,100 ft) is ~1,000 ft above the junction
results.evidence: The row itself is inconsistent (6,900 ft junction camp vs ~1,000 ft climb to a ~7,100 ft basin); one trip report puts a camp near the basin at 6,900 ft, which suggests the Fox Camp figure may be the basin's. No source giving Fox Camp's own elevation was found; left unpatched.
